Compare REST, GraphQL, and tRPC in a table highlighting speed, type-safety, and best use cases.

Here is a direct comparison between **REST**, **GraphQL**, and **tRPC** focusing on performance, type-safety, and ideal applications: ### Comparison Table | Feature / Metric | **REST** | **GraphQL** | **tRPC** | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Speed & Network Overhead** | • **Fast** execution on the server.
• Excellent built-in HTTP-level caching (CDN, browser).
• Risk of **over-fetching** or **under-fetching** data (multiple round trips). | • **Optimized payloads** (fetches only requested fields).
• Server overhead from parsing ASTs and resolving complex nested queries.
• HTTP-level caching is difficult (usually requires client-side caches like Apollo/Relay). | • **Very fast** and lightweight.
• Minimal serialization overhead (standard JSON/RPC over HTTP).
• Supports request batching out of the box.
• Standard HTTP caching possible with `GET` requests. | | **Type-Safety** | **Manual / Tool-dependent**
• Requires external tools (OpenAPI/Swagger) and codegen tools to generate client types.
• Types can fall out of sync easily without CI/CD validation. | **Schema-Driven**
• Strong schema definition language (SDL).
• Requires a build/code-generation step (e.g., GraphQL Code Generator) to create frontend types. | **Native End-to-End**
• 100% TypeScript inference.
• Types are shared directly from the backend to the frontend.
• **Zero code generation** required; changes reflect instantly in your IDE. | | **Data Fetching Paradigm** | Resource-based (`/users/:id/posts`) | Query-based (single endpoint `/graphql` with custom field selection) | Function-call/RPC-based (`trpc.user.getPosts.useQuery()`) | | **Language Ecosystem** | Language-agnostic (works with any language or client) | Language-agnostic (rich ecosystem across most languages) | **TypeScript only** (both frontend and backend must use TypeScript) | | **Learning Curve** | **Low** (industry standard, widely understood) | **High** (schemas, resolvers, N+1 problem, specialized caching) | **Low** (if already proficient in TypeScript) | | **Best Use Cases** | • Public-facing APIs and third-party integrations.
• Microservices architectures.
• Systems relying heavily on CDN/HTTP caching.
• Simple CRUD operations. | • Multi-platform apps (Web, iOS, Android) requiring different data shapes.
• Aggregating data from multiple microservices into a unified graph.
• Complex dashboards with deeply nested relations. | • Full-stack TypeScript applications (e.g., Next.js, Nuxt, T3 Stack).
• Internal SaaS apps and fast-moving startups.
• Monorepos where frontend and backend are maintained by the same team. | --- ### Quick Decision Guide * Choose **REST** if you are building a **public API**, need **native HTTP caching via CDNs**, or have diverse teams working in multiple programming languages (e.g., Go backend, Swift iOS app). * Choose **GraphQL** if you have **multiple client platforms** with drastically different data requirements or need to aggregate multiple backend data sources into a single schema. * Choose **tRPC** if you are working within a **full-stack TypeScript monorepo** and want the fastest possible development velocity with zero schema drift.
